title: Finite scalar local models have two-term finite-free sheaf resolutions
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $T$ any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Choose either $A=\mathcal O_E$, $\Lambda=\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, or $A=E$, $\Lambda=\underline E$, with the usual condensed coefficient rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. On the small pro-étale site of $T$ [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $B_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For an $A$-module $Q$, write $\underline Q$ for its constant module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], with the canonical map $\underline A\to B_T$. Let $P$ be a finitely presented $A$-module, meaning that it is the cokernel of a map $A^s\to A^t$ with $s,t$ finite, and put $L=B_T\otimes_{\underline A}\underline P$ [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor, sk-def-sfb-constructible]. There are finite nonnegative integers $a,b$ and an exact scalar sequence $0\to A^a\xrightarrow{u}A^b\xrightarrow{v}P\to0$ whose constant sheafification followed by extension of scalars yields an exact sequence of $B_T$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]
$$0\longrightarrow B_T^a\xrightarrow{1\otimes\underline u}B_T^b\xrightarrow{1\otimes\underline v}L\longrightarrow0.$$
Thus the augmented cochain complex $[B_T^a\to B_T^b]\to L[0]$, with free terms in degrees $-1,0$, is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. In the case $A=E$ one may take $a=0$, so $L$ is finite free. No Noetherianity assumption on $T$, torsion-freeness assumption on $P$, or completion of the derived category is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), proof: the finite projective scalar resolution for a finitely presented O_E-module, with Lemma 6.8.2(1) for the coefficient limit. Length-one finite-free strengthening for finite E/Q_ell; exact constant sheafification and scalar extension are Stacks sites-modules Tags 093J (lemma-constant-exact) and 093M (lemma-completion-flat).

proof.text: Prove the unit and associativity equations for scalarAction on pure tensors, scalar-map linearity by map_smul, the constant-functions ring equations before sheafification and their transport through the monoidal adjunction, and commutativity by braided constant sheafification. These proofs close the four auxiliary holes.

For integral scalars use the PID part of the extension-integers DVR theorem. A finite presentation gives a finite free surjection; its kernel is finite and free over the PID. A finite basis identifies it with the lifted finite-coordinate module. Over the field choose a finite basis directly and use a=0. These are scalar_resolution and field_scalar_sequence.

Use constantToContinuous_preservesFiniteLimits for the canonical scalar map, whose adjunction mate is constantFunctions by the equivalence triangle identity. Exactness of scalarModules is reflected by its forgetful functor. Exact monoidal constant sheafification, scalar extension, and inverse image from the point then give exactness of modelFunctor. Finite biproduct preservation, together with regularExtensionIso, gives the specified finite-free identifications.

Map the scalar short exact sequence through the exact model functor. Construct the two-term complex with HomologicalComplex.double and the augmentation with mkHomFromDouble. In degree minus one exactness is the monomorphism condition, in degree zero the cokernel augmentation is an isomorphism on homology, and all other degrees are zero. Thus the specified augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply this construction in both cases; the field basis isomorphism also gives finite freeness of the final model.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), with direct PID torsion-free flatness of the continuous coefficient presheaf in place of the completed-limit comparison; explicit categorical finite-biproduct and two-term homology constructions.

Statement and coefficient category: the statement keeps the discrete constant sheaf of A separate from B_T=p_T^*Lambda on the small pro-étale site, and L is the finite constant local model of sk-def-sfb-constructible, which is how the citer uses it. It is not a target, so there is no base-change morphism to compare. Step 1: the kernel is finitely generated by the relation images and torsion-free inside A^t; with the DVR lemma (PID plus local) this gives a finite free kernel. Step 2: the field-case basis argument is elementary. Steps 3-4: sheafification is exact and preserves finite products, and the unit/additivity of the relative tensor is elementary. Step 5: A is Noetherian as a PID, B_T is identified with the limit of the constant sheaves A/pi^n by det-prop (3), and 093M flatness applies. I checked the A-algebra compatibility of that identification; it is not automatic, since Galois-twisted reductions exist, and it follows from the representability in clauses (1)-(2), which the step uses as stated. Steps 6-7: the field case needs no flatness; H^{-1}=0 and H^0 is L through the augmentation. Small cases checked: P=0, P free, P=O_E/pi^n, s=0, field case; nothing is assumed on T. No cycle, and the dependency traversal does not reach the item. Duplicate search: lem-pur-constant-two-term-resolution covers only Z/l^N over Z_l, and det-lem-int-integral-heart-dualizable repeats the argument inside its proof but has no node for it, so there is no duplicate. lean.note: The integral and rational cases are the two conjuncts. Canonical constant-module and scalar-extension helpers belong to this local-model resolution and contain real data. HasResolution records the scalar sequence, its actual functorial image, both finite-free identifications, the component-normalized augmented complex, and QuasiIso of that augmentation. The rational case records a=0 and finite freeness of the final model explicitly.
